label: prop:neutron-proton-splitting
title: Neutron--proton mass splitting
html:
The model neutron-proton mass splitting derives from the quantum dilogarithm volumes:

  \Delta m := \alpha \cdot \lvert \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}) -
    \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) \rvert
  \approx 1.054 \; \mathrm{MeV}

where \Phi evaluates the respective quark ordering and \alpha = m_e \times 8G sets the binding scale.

Replacing one positive \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u} crossing with a negative \mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d} crossing causes the splitting. The \mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d} crossing carries more confinement energy. This makes the model neutron heavier. The volumes are evaluated with the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) at the proton value of q_0, pairing each strand with every later strand. With \alpha \approx 3.7449, \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) \approx -0.6149 and \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}) \approx -0.8964, the magnitude difference is \lvert\Delta\Phi\rvert \approx 0.2815 and the model value is 3.7449 \times 0.2815 \approx 1.0542 MeV.

Comparison with measurement. The CODATA 2022 splitting is m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}} \approx 939.56542194 - 938.27208943 = 1.29333251 MeV. The model value is about 18.5\% below it. This comparison is the empirical claim of the block; the mathematical statement is the model value only.
